ask_tools.name: web_search
ask_tools.description: Search the public web. Use it for what lies outside {{ORG_NAME}}: a project's documentation or current version, a vendor's limits or pricing, a public specification, the news. It knows nothing of {{ORG_NAME}}'s internal work, which the corpus tools cover. Returns results with a title, a url and a snippet; use web_fetch to read a page when the snippet is not enough.

query.description: What to search for, in natural language, with the distinctive terms.

topic.description: 'general' for most questions, 'news' for current events, 'finance' for markets where supported.

time_range.description: Only results published within this period before today. Use it for recent events; for anything that may be older, leave it out.

include_domains.description: Only results from these domains, such as ["docs.python.org"]. Empty searches everywhere.

exclude_domains.description: Leave out results from these domains.

ask_tools.name: web_fetch
ask_tools.description: Read one web page as Markdown. Use it on a web_search result when the snippet is not enough. By default it returns the page from the top. Providers with passage ranking use `query` to return relevant passages. Check the full page before drawing conclusions about missing details. `truncated` is set when a long page was cut. When the page cannot be read (a dead link, a block, a timeout), `ok` is false and `note` says why: use the search snippet and do not retry. Pages are large, so read the ones that matter.

url.description: The URL to read, usually from a web_search result.

query.description: What you are looking for on the page. Providers with passage ranking use this to return relevant passages. Omit it to get the page from the top.

ask_tools.name: code_search
ask_tools.description: Search the code of every repository in the code index. Use it for what the code says now: where something is defined, how a function works, which services read a configuration value, what produces an error message. The corpus tools cover what people said and decided; this covers what the code does. Each result is a file with its repo, path, and matching chunks with their line numbers and, when the index has one, a `url` to cite. Search for exact identifiers or distinctive strings, not descriptions, and narrow with repo:, file: or lang:. `total_matches` of 0 means no file has every term under these filters: drop a filter or a term once before concluding the code is not there. Use code_read when you need more of a file than the chunks show.

query.description: Terms match file content literally, ignoring case, and every term must match. They are not regular expressions: /Load.*Thread/ and (a|b) find nothing. Put a phrase in double quotes. Write a lowercase 'or' between alternatives and group with parentheses: (retry or backoff) timeout. Filters: repo:<regex> on the repository's full name, which starts with its host and owner, so write repo:billing-api or repo:billing-api$ and never repo:^billing-api; file:<regex> on the path; lang:<language>; sym:<name> for a symbol's definition. A leading - excludes: -file:test. Example: repo:billing-api lang:go "context deadline exceeded".

context_lines.description: Lines of context around each match.

ask_tools.name: code_read
ask_tools.description: Read the full content of ONE file from a repository in the code index (default branch, as of the last index). Use it when code_search chunks are not enough and you need the whole function, the imports or the surrounding logic. Pass repo and path exactly as a code_search result gives them. The result carries a `url` for the file, when the index has one, to cite, and `truncated` when a long file was cut. When the file is not in the index, `ok` is false: go back to the search results and do not guess another path. Files are large, so read the ones that matter.

repo.description: The repo of a code_search result, exactly as given.

path.description: The path of a code_search result, exactly as given.

pagerduty.label: API token
pagerduty.help: A PagerDuty REST API key that can write (Integrations, API Access Keys). Diderot reads incidents with it and adds its findings as notes.

pagerduty.label: Webhook signing secrets
pagerduty.help: The signing secret PagerDuty shows when you add a webhook subscription for incident.triggered. Point the subscription at this server's PagerDuty webhook port (9093 unless the deployment moves it), path /webhooks/pagerduty. To rotate it, enter the new and the old secret separated by a comma.

pagerduty.label: Notes posted as
pagerduty.help: The email of the PagerDuty user that Diderot's incident notes are posted as.

pagerduty.label: Alerts channel
pagerduty.help: The Slack channel where PagerDuty posts alerts: its name, its ID, or a link to it. Diderot replies in each alert's thread there, so invite it to the channel.

pagerduty.label: Alerts channel name
pagerduty.help: When set, Diderot replies only while the alerts channel has this name, so investigations can't go to a channel that was mistaken for it.

pagerduty.label: What investigations may read
pagerduty.help: What an investigation may search, one per line, such as public, internal, or slack-channel:C0123456789. Everyone in the alerts channel sees its answer, so list only what all of them may read.

sourcebot.label: Sourcebot URL
sourcebot.help: The address of your Sourcebot, such as https://sourcebot.example.com.

sourcebot.label: API key
sourcebot.help: A Sourcebot API key, from Settings, API keys in Sourcebot.

sourcebot.label: Repository prefix
sourcebot.help: The start that most repository names share, ending in /, such as github.com/example/. Ask shows names without it, which saves space in its answers. Leave empty to show full names.

sourcebot.label: What the code index covers
sourcebot.help: A phrase that tells Ask which code it can search. Ask reads it as "Search the code of …", so write, for example: every Example repository (public and private, indexed hourly). Leave empty for: every repository in the code index.

sourcebot.label: Where a file is read from
sourcebot.help: A phrase that tells Ask which version of a file it reads. Ask reads it as "Read the full content of one file from …", so write, for example: an Example repository (default branch, as of the last hourly index). Leave empty for: a repository in the code index (default branch, as of the last index).

tavily.label: Provider
tavily.help: Ask sends web searches and page fetches to this provider.

tavily.label: Kagi API key
tavily.help: From kagi.com/api/keys. Required when the provider is Kagi.

tavily.label: Tavily API key
tavily.help: Starts with tvly-. From your account at app.tavily.com. Ask's web searches are sent to Tavily with it. Required when the provider is Tavily.

tavily.label: Tavily API URL
tavily.help: Leave empty for Tavily's API. Set it only to send requests through a proxy.
